operations.description:
This endpoint allows new users to register as citizens by providing their email and password. Upon successful registration, a new record is created in the economic_board_citizens table with the provided email and a hashed password in the password_hash field. The created_at and updated_at fields are automatically set to the current UTC timestamp, and the status is initialized to 'active'. The deleted_at field remains null, indicating an active account.

The implementation follows strict security practices: passwords are never stored in plain text but are hashed using bcrypt before storage. The email field must be unique, as enforced by the GIN index on the economic_board_citizens table.

This registration flow enables citizens to participate in economic and political discussions by creating their persistent identity, linking future posts, comments, and attachments to this account. Success triggers issuance of a JWT access token and refresh token for subsequent authenticated requests.

This operation should be called before any other citizen-related operations, as it establishes the user's identity in the system. It is publicly accessible and does not require prior authentication.

operations.description:
This endpoint authenticates existing citizens by verifying their email and password against the records in the economic_board_citizens table. The system checks that the provided email exists and that the password_hash matches the bcrypt-hashed value provided.

When authentication succeeds, a new access token is generated and issued, along with a refresh token to enable token renewal. The updated_at field in the economic_board_citizens table is automatically updated to reflect the latest login timestamp, providing a security audit trail.

Login attempts for accounts with non-null deleted_at timestamps are rejected to prevent access to deleted accounts. Similarly, accounts with status of 'suspended' or 'banned' are denied access, enforcing the account status enforcement policy.

The system supports secure token refresh mechanisms and multiple concurrent sessions per citizen. This operation is essential for establishing a secure authenticated session and must be performed before accessing protected citizen resources.

This endpoint is public and does not require authentication prior to invocation as it is the entry point to the authentication system.

operations.specification: Citizen token refresh operation to obtain new access tokens using a valid refresh token, ensuring session continuity without requiring password re-entry.
operations.description:
This endpoint enables citizens to obtain new access tokens using a previously issued refresh token, extending their authenticated session without requiring password re-entry.

The system validates that the provided refresh token is active, unexpired, and correctly issued to the citizen identified in the token payload. This validation checks against stored refresh tokens associated with the citizen in the economic_board_citizens table's session management system.

Upon successful validation, a new access token is issued, and a new refresh token is rotated (replaced) to prevent replay attacks and enhance security. The refresh token is not stored directly in the economic_board_citizens table's plain fields but is managed securely in the backend token store linked by citizen_id.

This operation supports seamless user experience by maintaining authentication across application sessions or browser tabs, while maintaining high security through temporary access tokens and rotating refresh tokens.

This endpoint is public but requires a valid refresh token for access, not the citizen's password, ensuring that the authentication system remains secure even if access tokens are compromised.

The citizen_id field identifies the original author, and the post_id field references the published post this comment responds to. If the comment is part of a threaded conversation, the parent_comment_id field links to its parent comment.

Security: Any authenticated user may retrieve a comment by its ID. Moderators will receive escalated metadata fields including moderator_deleted_id. The operation respects comment deletion status: even deleted comments remain retrievable for audit and moderation purposes, but their status field will indicate 'deleted'. The comment body is always visible, regardless of status, to preserve context in moderation chains.

This operation directly maps to the economic_board_comments Prisma table. It returns all fields including status, which is critical for thread integrity and moderator audit trails. The comment must exist in the database to be retrievable; non-existent IDs return 404.

Related operations: Updates to a comment (PUT /comments/{commentId}) can modify the body and updated_at fields within 24 hours. Moderators can perform permanent deletion through a separate operation that sets status to 'deleted'.

Update the content of an economic board comment within the 24-hour editing window. This operation allows the original author to correct typographical errors, enhance clarity, or correct factual inaccuracies in their comment.

Only the citizen who originally created the comment may perform this update, verified through JWT authentication and citizen_id matching. The editor cannot change the related post_id, parent_comment_id, or citizen_id.

Only the body field may be modified. Other fields such as created_at, updated_at, status, and moderator_deleted_id are system-managed and will not be accepted in the request body. For comment updates, only a plain text string with maximum 500 characters is permitted, matching the constraint in the schema.

If the comment is published, the edit is immediately visible to all users. If the comment is deleted, updating it in the 24-hour window will not restore visibility, but will update the content field for moderator review and audit trail purposes. The updated_at field is automatically set to the current UTC timestamp with no user control.

This operation directly maps to the economic_board_comments Prisma table and respects its constraints, particularly the 500-character limit on the body field and the requirement that citizen_id must match the authenticated user. After 24 hours, the comment becomes immutable and this operation returns 403 Forbidden.

Related operations: Individual comments may be retired through moderator deletion (DELETE), but this endpoint only supports content edits, not moderation actions. Retrieval of the updated comment uses GET /comments/{commentId}.

The comment must exist and have status 'published'. Attempting to delete a comment that is already deleted or never published will return a 404 error. The operation does not change the comment's status flag but directly deletes the record from the database, which is consistent with the platform's policy for severe violations where audit trails must be maintained but content must be completely erased.

The comment's deletion is recorded in the economic_board_moderation_actions system as a deletion action, where the moderator and targeted citizen are logged for audit purposes. This operation complements the moderation action logging system by providing the actual data removal function.

This deletion operation is irreversible and should be used with extreme caution. It is not a soft delete - the comment cannot be restored once deleted. System logs preserve the timing and actor of deletion for compliance and forensic purposes. Related comments in reply threads are left intact as children of the deleted post remains visible with removed indicator.

It queries the economic_board_search_index and economic_board_search_metadata tables to deliver high-performance search results with filtering by status and topic tags. The search combines multiple data sources: full-text tokens from economic_board_search_index for keyword matching, and search metadata from economic_board_search_metadata for filtering by post status and creation date. The economic_board_search_tags table provides topic-based filtering through category associations, enabling users to refine results by economic topics such as "markets", "policy", or "regulation".

Perform a full-text search across economic board posts with advanced filtering capabilities.

This operation enables users to discover relevant discussions by querying multiple indexed data sources simultaneously: economic_board_search_index for full-text token matching, economic_board_search_metadata for filtering by post status and creation date, and economic_board_search_tags for category-based topic filtering.

The search supports complex and flexible querying, allowing users to combine keyword matches with filters for status (published, pending, rejected), publication time range, and specific economic topics. No separate endpoint for simple keyword searches is needed as this single endpoint handles all search scenarios, from basic text matching to sophisticated combinations with filters.

Results are returned in a paginated format optimized for display, with summary information including post titles, statuses, and topic tags. The operation avoids returning complete post content to maintain performance and reduce bandwidth usage. Full content can be retrieved individually using the GET /posts/{postId} endpoint.

The search functionality is crucial for platform usability, allowing citizens to find relevant economic discussions among thousands of posts. Performance is prioritized through denormalized search structures, ensuring results are returned under 2 seconds even with complex queries.

email.description:
Citizen's contact email address used for authentication and notifications. Must be unique and verified before posting content.

This field maps directly to the email column in the economic_board_citizens table. The system enforces uniqueness via a GIN index on this column. The email format must comply with RFC 5322 standards and will be validated during registration.

password.description:
Clear text password for authentication. The system will hash this value with bcrypt algorithm and compare against the password_hash in the economic_board_citizens table.

Passwords must be minimum 8 characters and include a mix of uppercase, lowercase, numeric and special characters as defined by the system's password policy. Client applications should never send pre-hashed passwords - this field must always contain plain text that the backend will securely hash.

This field directly corresponds to the password_hash column in the database, but with a user-friendly name for the API contract. Backend systems will handle the bcrypt hashing and salt generation.

ip.description:
Client IP address for session tracking. Optional field that can be provided by the client for SSR environments, though the server can extract this from the HTTP request context.

This field is used to populate the ip column in the economic_board_citizen_sessions table when creating a new session after registration or login. When provided by the client (e.g., in server-side rendering scenarios), it enhances the accuracy of the session audit trail. If not provided, the server will extract the client's IP address from the HTTP request headers, which is the standard and preferred approach in most deployment environments.

href.description:
Connection URL (current page URL) for session context in self-authentication operations. This field is mandatory for self-registration as it provides necessary context for session creation in the economic_board_citizen_sessions table.

This URL represents the page where the user initiated the registration process. It's required to support security auditing and fraud detection by tracking the origin of authentication requests. This field must always be a valid URL format (RFC 3986) and cannot be empty.

In web applications, this value is typically captured from window.location.href before the registration form is submitted.

referrer.description:
Referrer URL (previous page URL) for session context in self-authentication operations. This field is mandatory for self-registration as it provides necessary context for session creation in the economic_board_citizen_sessions table.

This URL represents the page the user was on immediately before navigating to the registration page. It aids in understanding user acquisition channels and detecting potential automated or suspicious registration patterns. The referrer must be a valid URL or an empty string if no referrer information is available (e.g., user typed URL directly).

This field is extracted from the HTTP Referer header in most cases but must be explicitly provided in SPA or mobile app environments.

IEconomicBoardCitizen.ICreate.description:
Registration data for creating a new citizen account.

Maps to the economic_board_citizens table for account creation. Only includes fields that can be provided by the client during registration: email and password (plain text).

Security rule: The password field must be plain text (never hashed) and will be hashed by the backend using bcrypt before storage in the password_hash column.

The email field must be unique and validated according to RFC 5322 standards. This requirement directly corresponds to the GIN index on the economic_board_citizens table.

No other fields (id, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at, status) can be provided by the client. These are system-managed fields set by the backend using the current UTC timestamp and default status 'active'.

The client inputs for ICreate can be mapped 1:1 to internal domain entity, with excludes for all system-managed fields and authentication context during creation.

This DTO represents the complete request body that must be received to create a citizen account. It enables atomic registration operation - all necessary data is provided in a single call, satisfying the atomic operation principle.

This type differs from ILogin because it is for registration (account creation), not authentication.

Security: This is a self-registration operation (join) where the actor is in the process of establishing their own identity, so session context fields (ip, href, referrer) are mandatory for session creation in the economic_board_citizen_sessions table.

Field mapping: This schema directly corresponds to the economic_board_citizens Prisma model's email and password_hash fields, with additional required session context fields for session tracking. All other fields are system-managed and excluded from this request type.

id.description:
The unique identifier of the authenticated citizen. This ID is pulled from the economic_board_citizens table and is used to identify the user across all authenticated operations.

This is a UUID-formatted string that serves as the primary key in the economic_board_citizens table. It is internally generated and never exposed to clients until after successful authentication. The ID is included in the JWT token payload and is used to establish the citizen's identity in subsequent API requests.

The ID field must be properly formatted as a UUID version 4 according to RFC 4122 standards.

IEconomicBoardCitizen.IAuthorized.description: Access and refresh tokens along with citizen identity after successful login or refresh. This schema defines the response body for both the /auth/citizen/login and /auth/citizen/refresh endpoints. The response contains the authenticated citizen's ID and a token object containing JWT access and refresh tokens that enable future authenticated operations. The refresh token is rotated on each refresh to enhance security. This structure follows the IAuthorizationToken definition exactly to maintain type safety and consistency across authentication responses.

email.description: Citizen's contact email address used for authentication and notifications. Must be unique and verified before posting content.

password.description: Clear text password for authentication. The system will hash this value with bcrypt algorithm and compare against the password_hash in the economic_board_citizens table.

refresh_token.description: The refresh token to be validated for generating new access tokens. This token must be currently valid and issued to the citizen currently attempting to refresh.

IEconomicBoardCitizen.IRefresh.description: Refresh token to be validated for generating new access tokens. This schema defines the request body for the /auth/citizen/refresh endpoint. The refresh_token is obtained during login or a previous refresh operation and is used to securely obtain a new access token without requiring the citizen to re-enter their password.

IEconomicBoardModerator.ICreate.description: Required information for creating a new moderator account, including a unique email address and a plain text password. The backend will hash this password before storing it in the password_hash field of the economic_board_moderators table.

IEconomicBoardModerator.IAuthorized.description: Authentication response containing only the authenticated moderator's unique identifier. Authentication tokens (access and refresh) must be transmitted via secure, HTTP-only cookies, never in the response body. This follows the zero-trust security model where identity is verified server-side from the JWT token.

This request body is used by the /economicBoard/moderator/moderators endpoint to filter and paginate moderator accounts. It specifies search terms, sorting preferences, and pagination controls.

IEconomicBoardModerator.IRefresh.description:
Refresh token issued during moderator authentication to enable secure token renewal.

This is a JWT refresh token that contains cryptographic authentication data, including the associated moderator_id and session expiration metadata. The refresh token is used exclusively in the POST /auth/moderator/refresh endpoint to obtain a new access token when the current one expires.

The token is stored in memory or secure server-side storage linked to the user's session record in the economic_board_moderator_sessions table.

On refresh request, the system validates:
- Token signature and integrity
- Session existence and non-expiration in economic_board_moderator_sessions
- Binding to the moderator_id in the token payload

The refresh token itself is NEVER stored in the database, only its associated session state is tracked.

After successful validation, the system generates a new access token and a new refresh token, invalidating the previous refresh token.

Must be presented in the request body as a raw string in RFC 7519 JWT format.

Note: This field should not be confused with the access token - the refresh token has a longer lifespan and can only be used once to obtain a new pair of tokens.

This design prevents stateful session storage while maintaining security through cryptographic binding and time-limited validity.
Must be included in the request body of POST /auth/moderator/refresh exactly as issued by the authentication service. No manipulation or decoding should be attempted by the client.

IEconomicBoardCategory.description:
System-defined categories for tagging and filtering discussion posts.

Contains the predefined set of topics used to classify and search content on the economic and political discussion board. These categories are immutable core system values that enable consistent tagging and filtering across the platform. Citizens can filter posts by these categories, and moderators use them to organize content.

Each category has a human-readable name and a unique code used in API calls and search queries. Change to this list requires administrator-level deployment and is not editable by users or moderators through the UI.

IEconomicBoardSystemConfig.description:
JSON-serialized value of the configuration setting (e.g., "500", "24", "true"). Can be string, number, boolean, or complex JSON object.

Note: This field represents the raw serialized value, not a parsed structural object. Clients should not assume any specific structure without knowledge of the corresponding key. The structure and meaning of this value is determined by the configuration key and should be handled according to application-specific serialization logic.

This is not a complex object type in the OpenAPI schema, but a simple string that may contain a JSON payload.

As a string type with no specific structure enforced in the OpenAPI spec, this allows maximum flexibility for configuration values while maintaining schema simplicity.

IEconomicBoardTimezoneSetting.description:
Defines the structure of a timezone setting with its attributes including name, code, offset, and default status.

This schema represents a timezone configuration for user-facing timestamp display. It contains the full timezone name from the IANA database (e.g., "Asia/Seoul"), a short platform identifier code (e.g., "KST", "EST"), the UTC offset, and a flag indicating whether it is the system default timezone. These settings ensure consistency in time representation across the platform by defining which valid timezones can be selected by users.

The system stores all timestamps internally in UTC, but uses these settings to present them in the user's local timezone for display purposes. Only timezone codes listed in this table are eligible for selection from the user interface. Where the system has a primary timezone defined (e.g., "Asia/Seoul"), the is_default flag ensures the correct base is applied.

This schema is consumed in the GET /economicBoard/settings/timezones/{timezoneCode} operation to return accurate timezone information based on the code parameter.

This type MUST be maintained through administrative interfaces as it directly affects time display for all users across the platform.

IEconomicBoardContentFlag.description:
Defines the structure of a content flag category used for automated and manual moderation.

This schema represents a specific classification of content violations that trigger moderation workflows. Each flag includes a machine-readable code used by detection systems, a human-readable name for administrative reference, a severity level to prioritize responses, a description of what constitutes a violation, and flags indicating whether automated detection and rejection are enabled.

The flag code serves as a stable reference for integration with moderation systems and API clients, ensuring consistency even if display names change. Different severity levels determine the aggressiveness of automated responses, with "high" severity flags potentially triggering immediate content removal.

This type is exclusively accessed by moderator-authorized endpoints to ensure system configuration integrity. It maps directly to the economic_board_content_flags table's fields, including auto_flag_enabled and auto_reject_enabled for integration with automated moderation processes.

When a post is flagged via user reports or system detection, the appropriate flag's configuration from this schema is applied to determine the moderation workflow and escalation hierarchy.

Complete detailed information about a specific economic board citizen

IEconomicBoardSearchMetadata.IRequest.description:
Parameters for performing a full-text search across economic board posts with advanced filtering capabilities.

This request object contains the search criteria used to query the index tables (economic_board_search_index and economic_board_search_metadata) and filter results by status and topic tags.

Search terms are provided as a keyword string which is matched against precomputed word vectors in the index. Filters allow refinement by post status ('published', 'pending', 'rejected') and by economic topics (categories) to return highly relevant results.

This request object does not include pagination parameters as pagination is handled at the interface layer via IPage wrapper. It also excludes any actor identifiers, as search is a public operation.

The actual keyword matching and relevance scoring are performed by the search engine based on tokenized content and frequency data stored in economic_board_search_index. Status and category filters are enforced in the database using economic_board_search_metadata and economic_board_search_tags.

This request object is only used in the PATCH /economicBoard/search endpoint which provides comprehensive search functionality in a single request.

Security: No authentication actor fields are included because search is a public-facing operation accessible without login. No sensitive user data can be queried through this endpoint.
